_about: Question contexts for generating reason sentences (plans/05 §7). Six per class. `chosen` is the answer a learner with that wrong belief gives; `correct` is what C really does. Contexts 1-4 of a class are train, 5 is val, 6 is test. The first context of each class is its trap item (03 §8.3); probe contexts come from 03 §6.3.

correct_rules.M01: `<=` includes the end value and `<` stops one before it; count every value the loop variable actually takes.
correct_rules.M02: A loop variable only changes when the code changes it; with no update the condition stays true forever.
correct_rules.M03: Setting or declaring the total inside the loop wipes it on every pass, so only the last pass counts.
correct_rules.M04: int divided by int drops the decimals before the result is stored, even when it is stored in a float.
correct_rules.M05: A local variable that was never given a value holds whatever was in memory, not 0.
correct_rules.M06: `=` stores the value and the condition then tests that stored value; `==` is the comparison.
correct_rules.M07: A `;` right after the if/for/while header is an empty body; the next statement is not part of it.
correct_rules.M08: Array indexes start at 0, so an array of n cells ends at index n-1.
correct_rules.M10: printf only shows the value on screen; the caller gets whatever `return` gives.
correct_rules.D01: `return` inside the loop ends the function at once, and an `else` that resets the flag overwrites an earlier match.
correct_rules.D02: `low = mid` keeps mid inside the window, so with neighbouring low and high the window never shrinks; it has to be `mid + 1`.
correct_rules.D03: After the first assignment the old value is gone, so both end up the same; a swap needs a temp.
correct_rules.D04: One pass only carries the biggest value to the end; the rest can still be out of order.
correct_rules.D05: Recursion only stops at a base case that returns without calling itself; without one it never stops.
correct_rules.D06: The argument has to change toward the base case; calling with the same or a growing value never reaches it.
correct_rules.D07: The value returned by the recursive call is thrown away unless the code uses it.
correct_rules.D08: `==` on strings or arrays compares addresses, not text; a char compared with a string literal is never equal.
